title: Left properness when every object is cofibrant
statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category in the terminology of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]; no simplicial enrichment is required. Suppose every object is cofibrant, meaning that its map from the initial object is a cofibration. Then $\mathcal M$ is left proper: for every cofibration $i:A\to B$ and weak equivalence $w:A\to A^{\prime}$, the induced map $B\to B\amalg_A A^{\prime}$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition A.2.4.2 and Lemma A.2.4.3 with its proof, printed pp. 814-815 (PDF pp. 832-833). Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this general model-category lemma.

proof.text: Fix a cofibration $i:A\to B$ and a weak equivalence $w:A\to A^{\prime}$. By the hypothesis, $A,B,A^{\prime}$ are cofibrant. The model-category convention in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] supplies all small colimits and the two weak factorization systems, without requiring enrichment. Every isomorphism lies in $W$: an isomorphism has the right lifting property against every cofibration (compose the bottom map of a lifting square with its inverse), hence belongs to $F\cap W$. In particular $1_A,1_B$ are weak equivalences. Form the two spans $S=(A\xleftarrow{1_A}A\xrightarrow{i}B)$ and $T=(A^{\prime}\xleftarrow{w}A\xrightarrow{i}B)$. The components $(w,1_A,1_B)$ give a map $S\to T$: on the left arrow commutativity is $w1_A=w$, and on the right it is $1_Bi=i1_A$.

source.place: Definition A.2.4.1 and Proposition A.2.4.2, printed p. 814; elementary preparation for the cube-lemma specialization.

proof.text: Apply clause (b) of [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison] to $S\to T$, with its variables $(X,A,B)=(A,A,B)$ and $(X^{\prime},A^{\prime},B^{\prime})=(A^{\prime},A,B)$. All six objects are cofibrant, both designated right legs are the given cofibration $i$, and the three component maps are $w,1_A,1_B$, which are weak equivalences by step 1. The model-category convention is the same complete and cocomplete, functorial two-WFS convention as in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. In particular this comparison has no properness hypothesis and requires no condition that the left legs be cofibrations. It gives a weak equivalence $u:Q\to P$, where $Q=A\amalg_A B$ is the pushout of $(1_A,i)$ and $P=A^{\prime}\amalg_A B$ is the pushout of $(w,i)$. If $a:A\to Q,b:B\to Q$ and $a^{\prime}:A^{\prime}\to P,b^{\prime}:B\to P$ are the coprojections, then $ua=a^{\prime}w$ and $ub=b^{\prime}$, by the meaning of the induced map.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.6 (cube lemma), printed pp. 126-127, specialized to the map of spans with components (w, identity, identity).

proof.text: The colimit universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies $b:B\to Q$ as an isomorphism. Indeed the maps $i:A\to B$ and $1_B:B\to B$ give a unique $h:Q\to B$ with $ha=i$ and $hb=1_B$. The pushout relation says $a=bi$, so $bh$ agrees with $1_Q$ after both $a$ and $b$; uniqueness gives $bh=1_Q$. The isomorphism argument in step 1 therefore makes $b$ a weak equivalence, and step 2 then makes $ub=b^{\prime}:B\to P$ a weak equivalence. The pushout written as $B\amalg_A A^{\prime}$ has the same universal property with the two legs interchanged. The unique maps in both directions preserving the coprojections are inverse by uniqueness, so give an isomorphism $c:P\to B\amalg_A A^{\prime}$. The same isomorphism argument in step 1 makes $c$ a weak equivalence, and two-out-of-three makes $cb^{\prime}$ one too. Because $c$ preserves the $B$ coprojection, $cb^{\prime}$ is precisely the map required in the item. Since $i,w$ were arbitrary, the defining left properness condition holds.

source.place: Definition A.2.4.1 and Proposition A.2.4.2, printed p. 814; pushout identification by its universal property.
